parsed.why: Gender-marker change only via litigation, no statutory procedure, but courts have repeatedly ruled for trans applicants and employment protection names gender identity. Visitor exposure mostly indirect; discrimination reported but no documented state targeting of visitors. Elevated-to-reduced band.

Cross-dressing provision (Art. 152) and sodomy law, with documented state violence including extrajudicial killings against LGBTQ people, no legal gender recognition, and no protective machinery. Gender presentation itself falls within criminal scope; severe, near-severe-risk tier.

No criminalisation of gender identity, incitement law covers gender identity, and the society is described as broadly neutral. But employment protection was repealed, no legal recognition or trans protections exist, and an unevidenced prison and documentation gap remains. Elevated band.

Documented state targeting: police mass detentions of trans women for ID checks, a custody death of a trans prisoner, birth-sex prison placement, strip searches, and escalating official hostility with 2025-26 legislative drift. Severe-to-high risk band.

Decriminalised, explicit national gender-identity anti-discrimination law and hate-crime enhancements in some regions. But documented Pride violence in the capital, hostile surveys, and a formal gender-recognition regime that is discriminatory. Visitor exposure is elevated, not reduced.
